summary.headline: Hexaware Q3 CY26 revenue rose 1.6% QoQ to $411.9M, below plan; adjusted EBIT margin 13.8%; no current-quarter guidance given.
summary.overview: Hexaware's Q3 CY26 (quarter ended September 2026) revenue was $411.9M, up 1.6% QoQ and 4.3% YoY, which management called below its own expectations due to a GSE client slowdown and delayed large-deal ramps. Adjusted EBIT margin was 13.8% (reported 12.2%) after 160 bps of one-offs including the Netherlands restructuring, earn-out reversals and CEO transition. The company narrowed its CY26 adjusted EBIT margin guidance to 13% to 13.5% and declined to give a Q4 outlook. New CEO Vivek Jetley, in his first call, committed to a 90-day strategy review and tighter forecasting process.

segments.name: Financial Services
segments.commentary: Grew 3.0% QoQ and 2.4% YoY; a GSE client under cost optimisation is a headwind expected to persist in Q4, so FY growth expected below company average.

segments.name: Healthcare & Insurance
segments.commentary: Declined 40 bps QoQ on lower asset revenue but grew 6.3% YoY; management expects it to be among the strongest YoY drivers for FY, though decisions have been delayed in H&I.

segments.name: Manufacturing & Consumer
segments.commentary: Grew 1.8% QoQ and 3% YoY, fifth consecutive quarter of YoY growth; deal closures converting to revenue.

segments.name: Professional Services
segments.commentary: Broadly stable QoQ (normal seasonality after strong Q2 from largest client); 7.8% YoY growth.

segments.name: Banking
segments.commentary: Grew 6.6% QoQ and 13.5% YoY; management expects a strong Q4 and full year.

segments.name: Travel & Transportation
segments.commentary: Declined 3.5% QoQ and 8.5% YoY on end-client softness and Middle East conflict; expected soft for full year.

segments.name: TPP (Technology Products & Platforms)
segments.commentary: Grew 7.2% QoQ and 9.7% YoY; reported separately since this year on a smaller base.

segments.name: Geographies
segments.commentary: Americas +1.5% QoQ, +1.1% YoY; Europe +3.1% QoQ, +12.8% YoY; Asia Pacific +20% YoY, with GTT softness in APAC from the Middle East situation.

guidance_outlook: No guidance given for Q4 CY26; management says Q4 will follow the usual seasonal pattern with furloughs and fewer working days causing a sequential decline.
CY26 adjusted EBIT margin narrowed to 13% to 13.5% (within the previously communicated range).
Q4 margins to face seasonal headwinds and a ~100 bps merit increase effective October 1, partly offset by better realisation, operational improvements and Netherlands closure uplift.
Netherlands restructuring expected to add ~40 bps to annual operating margin; no incremental charges from next quarter, with full completion by Q2 CY27.
Hedge and translation losses estimated at ~$4M and ~$3M in the next two quarters.
Normalised full-year effective tax rate expected at 25-26%.
Management to share strategic plan and FY priorities with full-year results; will provide outlook once confident.
capex_capacity: Netherlands operations restructured in Q3 at ~$6M one-off cost (~150 bps at PBT level); expected to add ~40 bps to annual operating margin.
Anthropic partnership: about 1,200 Hexawarians certified; on track for 250 FTEs and 1,000 AI architects by mid next year; new Anthropic unit being established.
Zero Friction Enterprise and Zerovity AI platform launched; eight customers have moved workloads to AI-native or cloud-native environments.
Utilization 84.9%, expected to stay range-bound; DSO expected range-bound through year-end.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth below plan due to a GSE client's cost optimisation, and delayed closures and slower ramp in large deals concentrated in H&I and Travel & Transportation; one rebadging account ramping slower.
Management says the pipeline remains strong, with some deals expected to close in Q4 and others in Q1 CY27.
Vendor consolidation: about 13 large clients went through it; most outcomes favourable, one pending and one negative.
Pricing: management acknowledged pricing pressure in initial project phases, with AI productivity to support margins over the project lifecycle; outcome-based pricing emerging in TPP deals.
Asset revenue about 2% of full-year revenue, ranging 1.5% to 2.5% in any quarter; Q3 included a headwind from lower asset revenue.
Sales incentives: hunting team moved from quota-based to commission-based plan earlier this year; to be reviewed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add or double down on service lines or verticals, and change sales incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: New CEO will run a 90-day strategy review covering where to play, competition, go-to-market and delivery focus, and investments; hunting team already moved to commission-based pay.

qa_highlights.question: With Q3 at 1.7% growth, what Q4 traction would be needed to meet the ~6-7% guidance, which implies a 4-5% ask rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number and said Q4 should follow the usual seasonal sequential decline from furloughs and fewer working days.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue impact from liquidating Mobiquity Netherlands?
qa_highlights.answer: Marginal revenue impact, as work had already moved offshore; restructuring was needed because costs could not be cut in line with declining revenue under Dutch labour law.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q3 miss a broad-based slowdown in deal ramps or client-specific, and how to assess the momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ramp delay is one account only (rebadging deal) and the pipeline and momentum are intact; deals slipped into Q4 or Q1 due to client decision cycles.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a process change needed after repeated guidance misses?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Jetley said he is still reviewing root causes; will tighten the sales-to-forecast process and expand safety margins in forecasts.

qa_highlights.question: How are the recent acquisitions (SMC, CyberSolve) performing and what drove the earn-out adjustments?
qa_highlights.answer: SMC (GCC capability) fell short of year-two targets, giving a 530 bps earn-out reversal as clients slowed GCC setups amid AI; CyberSolve outperformed, causing a 110 bps extra charge. Net 420 bps credit in other income, offset by 140 bps amortisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the growth slowdown due to weak demand and aggressive competitor bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed slowdown mainly to vendor consolidation and client-specific timing; said it is a buyer's market with pricing pressure in initial phases, but incumbents tend to lose more than challengers.

risks_watch: Q4 CY26 sequential decline expected seasonally, with no formal guidance; ability to hit the revised trajectory is uncertain.
Delayed deal closures in H&I and Travel & Transportation; Middle East conflict affecting T&T and APAC.
GSE client cost optimisation in FS continues to weigh into Q4; FS full-year growth below company average.
Margin headwinds from Q4 seasonality and the 100 bps merit increase; utilisation range-bound.
Earn-out and acquisition accounting volatility (SMC shortfall, CyberSolve outperformance) and hedge losses of ~$4M and ~$3M in next two quarters.
New CEO's strategic plan, expected in about 90 days, and revised forecasting process to be tested in the next call.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious: management acknowledged Q3 revenue was below expectations and withheld Q4 guidance while the new CEO reviews strategy and forecasting. It was confident on pipeline health, AI positioning and margin range narrowing, but gave few specifics on timing of deal closures.

growth.why: No revenue growth guidance or Q4 outlook was given; management cut the CY26 adjusted EBIT margin range to 13–13.5%, said Q3 revenue of $411.9M (+4.3% YoY) was below expectations, and backed the pipeline only with vague deal-closure timing, with no capacity additions.

mgmt.note: Vivek Jetley became CEO and joined on this first call; he committed to a 90-day strategy review and tighter forecasting, with the strategic plan to be shared with full-year results.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Zero Friction Enterprise and Zerovity AI platform have launched with eight customers migrating workloads, and the Anthropic unit is being set up with 250 FTEs and 1,000 AI architects targeted by mid next year, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Delayed large-deal closures convert in Q4 CY26 / Q1 CY27
rows.why: Management says some deals will close in Q4 and others in Q1 CY27, but gave no firm timing and the H&I decisions have been delayed.

rows.label: New CEO 90-day strategy review and forecasting reset
rows.why: CEO Vivek Jetley committed to a 90-day strategy review and a tighter sales-to-forecast process with wider safety margins, with the plan to be shared at full-year results.

rows.label: Netherlands restructuring completion
rows.why: The restructuring cost ~$6M, is expected to add ~40 bps to annual operating margin, and will be fully completed by Q2 CY27 with no incremental charges after this quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on pipeline health, AI positioning and the Netherlands margin uplift, but cautious on Q4 and gave no revenue guidance; analysts pressed on repeated guidance misses, the Q4 ask rate, and whether the slowdown is broad-based or client-specific.
